chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him):
Regarding the female slave whom a man buys while she is pregnant, he said: 'He should not approach her until she gives birth to her child.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man buying a pregnant female slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Reported from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), this hadith establishes the ruling of *Istibra'* (waiting period) for a pregnant slave woman, mandating that her owner refrain from sexual intimacy until she delivers. This ensures the clarity of lineage (*Luquh*) and prevents confusion regarding paternity, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence for determining the status of the child as free or slave.
